patch_description:
The previous program failed validation because its recursive value-grouping pipeline produced inconsistent shapes/orderings: it split into `grouped_rows`/`remaining_rows` and recombined DataFrames via `pd.concat`/`update` with positional `loc[i]` inserts, dropped/merged columns, appended an `original_index` helper column, sorted rows, and finally returned an empty `column_orderings` list — so per-row column orderings were not consistent with the returned data (and cell/shape preservation assertions could fail on mixed-type data). The whole approach also optimized squared field lengths on a single "max group value" rather than actual character-prefix reuse.

Fix: replace the editable block with a correct, bounded construction-selection algorithm.
- Serialize each cell exactly as the evaluator does (missing → ""), factorize columns once into integer codes, and precompute value lengths.
- Build up to three cheap per-row column-ordering candidates: (1) a global frequency-ranked order scoring each column as sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), (2) the original column order, and (3) a recursive conditional partition tree that picks, inside each row group, the remaining column with the largest length-weighted pair repetition, partitions rows by that column's codes, and orders suffixes per group (bounded depth 8, bounded candidate columns, deterministic global-order tail).
- Score candidates with the exact serial Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of the sorted serialized rows, using C-speed slice-equality binary search), pick the best; skip scoring with a safe heuristic fallback when the data is too large.
- One-way dependencies are enforced by moving each dependent column right after its source in every row order; col_merge groups are merged into a single concatenated column (serialization is unchanged since fields have no separators), preserving API semantics.
- The output DataFrame keeps the original row order/index, object dtype, and returns per-row column name orderings matching the positional data exactly, with no fabricated, dropped, or altered cells.
